development.developer: Sim Lian (Treasure) Pte Ltd — Sim Lian Group (mass-market/value builder; also Tampines Trilliant, Centrale 8)
development.address: 15-71 Tampines Lane / Tampines Street 11, S52xxxx (former Tampines Court en-bloc site)
development.orientation_notes: Huge triangular 6ha site, 29 identical 12-storey blocks in 3 long ROWS running roughly east-west, so the vast majority of units face NORTH or SOUTH (good — avoids direct E/W sun on the broad face). PIE (Pan Island Expressway) + its slip roads run along the entire NORTH/NW top edge. Tampines Lane runs along the EAST/SE edge (open green field beyond). Tampines Street 11 runs along the SOUTH edge and carries the MAIN entrance + arrival court. Open field to the WEST. Treasure Clubhouse sits dead-center; three 50m lap pools + facilities fill the spines between the rows. THREE ROWS: (1) TOP/NORTH row blocks 43,45,47,49,51,53,55,57 — north face -> PIE expressway (noise, but north = no sun, green buffer); south face -> 50m lap pool (quiet, premium). (2) MIDDLE row blocks 15,17,19,21,23,25,27,29,31,33,35 — face internal lap pools/clubhouse on BOTH sides = best privacy, best views, buffered from expressway and road. (3) BOTTOM/SOUTH row blocks 1,3,5,7,9,11,13 — north face -> lap pool (good); south face -> Tampines Street 11 (road noise/arrival activity but nearest the entrance). WEST-END blocks (55,57,15,13,9) and their west-corner stacks take the worst afternoon sun + face open field/PIE merge. EAST-END blocks (37,41,31,33,35,1) get morning sun and face Tampines Lane / open green (open outlook, minor road).
known_issues: 2,203 units across 29 blocks = one of SG's largest condos. Deep resale liquidity BUT perpetual internal resale supply that structurally caps per-unit pricing power / appreciation.
Poor MRT walk: ~1.1km / 13 min to Simei (EW3); Tampines West (DT31) ~0.99km. No station at the doorstep. Weak for a 1BR tenant profile.
North-edge (top-row) stacks facing the PIE take expressway noise; reviewers call it audible but usually tolerable.
Tight 3-row layout: the MAJORITY of units face another block directly -> privacy is the project's headline weakness (StackedHomes).
West-corner stacks take heavy afternoon sun.
Mixed management/customer-service feedback; '1+Study' and studio-1BR layouts criticised (study is a desk niche; 1BR lacks a proper dividing wall).
0-5yr post-TOP window (2023) — the cohort that historically underperforms on forward returns while amortising launch premium (mitigant: launched cheap ~$1,346psf so premium was small).

~63sqm, most numerous 2-bed type; deepest resale demand band.
~155-160sqm; largest format. No penthouses, no dual-key.

facing_map.best: Middle-row blocks (15,17,19,21,23,25,27,29,31,33,35) facing the internal 50m lap pools — pool view, buffered from both expressway and road. Stack 25 singled out as best-privacy (faces clubhouse, not another block). South-face units of the top row (43-57) also enjoy quiet pool views.
facing_map.avoid: West-corner stacks (afternoon sun): 123,117,116,110,7,1,92,26,27,79,186,187,199 per StackedHomes. North-face top-row stacks directly fronting the PIE (expressway noise). South-face bottom-row stacks directly on Tampines Street 11 (road/arrival noise). Any ground-floor/PES stack (low-floor, faces landscaping/walkway).
facing_map.note: Listings on PropertyGuru rarely publish the stack/unit number, so a specific listing can usually only be tied to its LAYOUT TYPE (via sqft) and to the SET of stacks carrying that facing — not to one stack — unless the listing text names a block/floor/facing.
